subject: Post-demo: geocontrol, cross-region backups & logging retention
messages:
From: Olivia Yang <olivia.yang@medexa.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paul Turner <paul.turner@medexa.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — geocontrol & data handling questions

Thanks again for the demo today — great overview. A few follow-up items from my security / infra team so we can qualify internally and prepare the procurement packet. I’ve grouped them by priority: 

1) PII in requests and model data handling
- Do you persist full request payloads by default? If so, what fields are redacted and what retention window is applied?
- Can we opt-out of retention for certain routes (e.g., HIPAA workflows)?

2) Logging and audit trails
- What logs are kept (request/response tokens, metrics, system logs)?
- Can logs be exported automatically to our S3 bucket and how long do you retain on your side before export?

3) Region pinning / cross-region failover
- If we pin a model to the EU region, what happens during a regional outage? Is cross-region failover automatic or manual?
- If failover occurs, do you keep data residency guarantees (e.g., do we get an opt-in/out for cross-border failover)?

4) Backups and snapshots
- Frequency of snapshots and whether backups are cross-region replicated; RTO/RPO targets for Dedicated and Private setups.

5) Encryption & key management
- Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM? Full-disk and in-flight encryption details appreciated.

Attached: our internal SOC2 extract with questions (medexa-soc2-questions.pdf) — we can prioritize answers we need for our security review.

Would like a short written reply for procurement (1–2 pages) and then a 30-minute follow-up call with engineering to validate the answers.

—Olivia
Olivia Yang
Head of IT, Medexa Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — geocontrol & data handling questions

Thanks Olivia — helpful list. High-level answers below; Ben/Karthik are looped in for the technical specifics and we'll follow up with a short call. Attached is a brief geocontrol summary for your SOC reviewer (redwood-geocontrol-summary.xlsx).

Quick answers:
- Persistence & PII: By default we retain full request/response payloads for 30 days for hosted API customers (configurable). We support route-level opt-out of payload retention for sensitive routes and can configure masking/redaction rules during onboarding for Dedicated/Private deployments.

- Logging & exports: We keep operational logs (aggregated metrics) and optional request-level logs (token-level traces) if enabled. Logs can be streamed/exported to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets; default retention on our side is 30 days unless you request longer retention or immediate export.

- Region pinning & failover: You can pin models to a region. During regional outages we support policy-driven failover: automatic (with opt-in for cross-border) or manual (operator-initiated). For EU-pinned workloads we offer an opt-in cross-border failover that requires explicit approval and audit logging.

- Backups: Snapshot cadence and cross-region replication depend on deployment: Hosted — managed snapshots every 12 hours with warm-standby options; Dedicated/Private — configurable snapshot frequency and optional cross-region replication. RTO/RPO vary by plan; we’ll include numbers in the follow-up.

- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated & Private. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS with customer-side key wrapping options.

Next steps: 
1) Ben/Karthik to provide a 1–2 page technical appendix addressing retention windows, exact log types, and RTO/RPO by deployment.
2) Schedule 30-min engineering sync — proposed times: Tue 12/1 09:00–11:00 PT or Tue 12/1 14:00–16:00 PT. Please confirm a slot.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 3:12 PM Olivia Yang <olivia.yang@medexa.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo today — great overview. A few follow-up items from my security / infra team so we can qualify internally and prepare the procurement packet. I’ve grouped them by priority:
> 
> 1) PII in requests and model data handling
> - Do you persist full request payloads by default? If so, what fields are redacted and what retention window is applied?

Short technical appendix (summary):
- Payload retention: Hosted default = 30d; Dedicated = customer-configurable at provisioning (0d–365d). Route-level opt-out supported via a per-route retention flag. For HIPAA-sensitive routes we can set retention to 0d and enable immediate streaming-only mode.

- Redaction: We provide a configurable redaction pipeline (regex + keyed rules) that runs before any storage. We can redact by JSON path, header, or model-output token category.

- Logs: Two classes — operational (aggregates, metrics, infra traces) and request-level (request headers, token counts, optionally token-streams if enabled). Request-level logs are off by default for Hosted; can be enabled with explicit consent and are retained based on the chosen retention window. Logs can be exported via S3/GCS or pushed to Splunk/Datadog.

- Exports & retention timing: Export jobs run as near-real-time streams or batch (hourly). Our side retention is configurable; we recommend immediate export to your bucket for long-term retention policies.

- Failover behavior: Policy-driven. For EU-pinned workloads you can choose: 1) no cross-border failover (requests queue/fail) 2) manual failover only 3) automatic failover with explicit audit/consent per failover event. Warm-standby uses snapshot replication; cold-standby requires longer RTO.

- Snapshots & RPO/RTO (examples): Hosted standard — snapshots every 12 hours, RPO ~12h, RTO ~1h (cold switch to warm); Dedicated — snapshots configurable to 1h/6h/12h, typical RPO 1–6h depending on plan, RTO ~30–60m for warm-standby. Private on-prem — dependent on customer infra.

- Encryption/KMS: Customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS / GCP KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private; HSM integration available for enterprise. In-flight TLS 1.3, at-rest AES-256.

Attachments: redwood-geocontrol-summary.xlsx (short matrix showing failover modes + retention knobs).

If useful I can put the concrete RTO/RPO numbers for the Dedicated commitment tiers into the appendix before our call.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
